content: 1. Ozanimod has immunosuppressive effects, which may increase the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are advised when co-administering with other immunosuppressive therapies, as this combination may lead to additive immune effects during treatment and in the weeks following administration. When transitioning from drugs with prolonged immune effects, the half-life and mechanism of action of these drugs should be considered to avoid unintended additive immunosuppressive effects. 2. Ozanimod and antithymocyte globulin (rabbit) may enhance each other's immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with immunosuppressive therapies may result in additive immune effects during and after treatment. When switching from drugs with prolonged immune effects, consider their half-life and mechanism of action to prevent unintended additive immunosuppression. 3. Ozanimod and apomorphine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, ozanimod treatment should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently receiving QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 4.
